s: Idempotency, rate limiting, pagination, error handling, versioning
d: Good API design makes your service easy to use, debug, and scale. Patterns like idempotency keys, consistent error formats, rate limiting, and proper versioning separate professional APIs from amateur ones.
c: Rate limiting strategies (token bucket, sliding window)

p: Good API design means creating interfaces that are predictable, versioned, and easy for clients to consume. It involves consistent naming conventions, pagination, filtering, and thorough documentation.
1. Use plural nouns for resources (/users, not /user).

// Pagination Example
app.get('/api/v1/posts', async (req, res) => {
  const limit = parseInt(req.query.limit) || 10;
  const page = parseInt(req.query.page) || 1;
  const posts = await db.posts.find().skip((page-1)*limit).limit(limit);
  res.json({ data: posts, page, limit });
});

API URL Structure:
[Base URL]       [Version] [Resource] [Identifier] [Sub-resource]
api.example.com /v1       /users     /123         /orders
-> "Get orders for user 123 using API version 1"
